# Linnet of Primary Care (`linnet-of-primary-care`)

Checks advanced primary care management (APCM, G0556 to G0558) each month: codes billed for patients not enrolled or with no consent, billed twice, billed with care management codes the rules do not allow in the same month, billed at a level the patient record does not support, and enrolled patients not billed. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Linnet never submits or changes claims. Linnet never enrolls patients or records consent.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Care management and value-based care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y linnet-of-primary-care demo
npx -y linnet-of-primary-care mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up primary care practice, made-up patients. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`apcm-enrolled.csv`](fixtures/apcm-enrolled.csv) and [`claims-2026-10.csv`](fixtures/claims-2026-10.csv) for October 2026. Planted:
  - N1: three chronic conditions but billed G0556 (the record points to G0557).
  - N2: G0557 and 99490 (chronic care management) in the same month.
  - N3: G0557 with no consent on file.
  - N4: G0557 billed twice in October.
  - N5: G0556 billed for a patient not on the APCM list.
  - N6: enrolled and consented as QMB, nothing billed (G0558 expected).
  - N7: G0558 with an office visit the same month is fine. N8 left the program in August and is not expected.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): example rates. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

`npx -y linnet-of-primary-care demo` runs the agent on the fictional files in [`fixtures/`](fixtures) in a temporary folder. Captured output:

Files: kestrel-out/linnet/linnet-apcm.csv, kestrel-out/linnet/linnet-apcm.html.

  status: blocked  decision: block
  reason: Linnet never enrolls patients or records consent.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `linnet_check` | List enrollment and consent problems, double billing, conflicting codes, wrong levels and enrolled patients not billed. | runs |
| `linnet_write_report` | Write linnet-apcm.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and linnet-apcm.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/linnet). | runs |
| `linnet_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `linnet_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `linnet_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `linnet_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Linnet never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `patient_enroll` | Linnet never enrolls patients or records consent. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `linnet_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `patients` (required) | APCM enrollment list under --root: patient, chronic condition count, QMB, tier, consent date, enrolled and disenrolled dates |
| `claims` (required) | Claim lines for the month: patient, date of service, code, units |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: rates, conflict_codes |
| `month` (required) | Month to check, YYYY-MM |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx linnet-of-primary-care inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### APCM enrollment (`patients`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` (required) | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `conditions` | number | Chronic Conditions, Conditions, Condition Count, Number of Conditions |
| `qmb` | text | QMB, Qualified Medicare Beneficiary, QMB Status |
| `tier` | text | Tier, APCM Level, APCM Code, Level |
| `consent_date` | date | Consent Date, Consent, APCM Consent, Consent Signed |
| `start` | date | Enrolled, Enrollment Date, Start, Start Date |
| `end` | date | Disenrolled, End, End Date, Termed |

### Claims (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |

## Settings file (`linnet_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `rates` | Expected payment by code, for dollar estimates |
| `conflict_codes` | Codes not billed in the same month as APCM; replaces the default list (CCM, PCM, TCM) |

## Memory

`linnet_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `linnet_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "linnet-of-primary-care": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "linnet-of-primary-care",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add linnet-of-primary-care -- npx -y linnet-of-primary-care mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
linnet-of-primary-care tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
linnet-of-primary-care sources               # the columns each input is read from
linnet-of-primary-care inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
linnet-of-primary-care call linnet_check '{"patients":"<patients>","claims":"<claims>","month":"<month>"}'
linnet-of-primary-care eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
linnet-of-primary-care demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
